Back up and restore Postgres 9.6 through 17 clusters: base backups and the WAL archive, each in a set of its own

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres <command>
```

## postgres archive

copy a finished WAL file into the spool; set archive_command = 'goback postgres archive --spool DIR %p %f'

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres archive [flags] <path> <name>
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--spool value` | directory archive_command copies WAL files into and the WAL backup commits from | `GOBACK_POSTGRES_SPOOL` |  |

## postgres base

pg_basebackup connects as libpq does: through --dbname, or through PGHOST, PGUSER and the
other PG* variables. The user needs the REPLICATION attribute.

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres base [flags]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dbname value` | connection string pg_basebackup connects with | `GOBACK_POSTGRES_DBNAME` |  |
| `--pg-basebackup value` | the pg_basebackup to run; its major version must match the server's | `GOBACK_POSTGRES_BASEBACKUP` | `pg_basebackup` |

## postgres restore

restore_command runs goback again for every WAL file Postgres asks for: this binary with the
global flags given here, unless --goback names another command. Flags end up in
postgresql.auto.conf, or recovery.conf before Postgres 12; settings from the environment have to
be in Postgres's environment.

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres restore [flags] <data directory>
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--base-set value` | set the cluster's base backups go to; digits name it by id, from the set's head rather than the index |  |  |
| `--wal-set value` | set the cluster's WAL goes to, for recovering past the end of the base; digits name it by id, as --base-set |  |  |
| `--at value` | moment to recover to, as RFC 3339 (2026-10-02T14:30:00Z); the end of the WAL set when empty |  |  |
| `--goback value` | command restore_command runs goback as, global flags included |  |  |

## postgres wal

commit the spooled WAL files to the set named by --set, then delete them from the spool

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres wal [flags]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--spool value` | directory archive_command copies WAL files into and the WAL backup commits from | `GOBACK_POSTGRES_SPOOL` |  |
| `--base-set value` | set the cluster's base backups go to |  |  |
| `--window value` | how far back point-in-time recovery reaches; WAL older than the oldest base backup inside it is let go |  | `336h0m0s` |

## postgres wal-get

write a WAL file of a WAL commit to a path, as restore_command

```sh
goback [global flags] postgres wal-get [flags] <%f> <%p>
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--wal-set value` | set the WAL commit belongs to |  |  |
| `--commit value` | the WAL commit, in hex |  |  |
